The outside-operator round in the visual plant

Apinan Soottitantawat
Department of Chemical Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Chulalongkorn University

Three parts

What we will answer

1What does the outside operator see on the round?→ 2What does each field reading tell you?→ 3How are hand valves and field checks handled on the round?→

RDC = rotating-disc contactor; TCE = 1,1,2-trichloroethane; OTS = operator training simulator; DCS = control system; EL = elevation above grade, m; NO / NC = normally open / closed; LO / LC = locked (car-sealed) open / closed; CD = closed drain; PSV = relief valve; AH = analyzer shelter. Tags use ISA letters: F flow, T temperature, P pressure, L level, S speed, J power, V vibration, A analyzer, H hand; then I indicator, T transmitter, DT differential transmitter, C controller, V valve; SLL / SHH = low-low / high-high trips.

Group overview · Operate

Where Visual plant 3D sits in its group

The group asks: How do I run C-101: what do I see and move on the console, what does the SIS allow or stop, what must be done and checked outside, where is it in the plant, and how is it all connected?

  1. Needs before it startsLayout (stations, platform, hand valves), the P&ID tags, the live model
  2. Hands onRounds sheet (28 rows checked within 3 %), identification score (target 90 %), hand-valve positions → P&ID
  3. When in a projectConstruction and start-up, Operation and change

The Operate overview tab, first in the group, shows the whole chain with one worked thread.

Why this order

The round follows the process

Stations and pictures in hand, the order of the walk comes from the flow.

  1. Stations 1–4: solvent sideD-102, P-102A/B, E-102 and FV-103
  2. Stations 5–7: feed sideT-101, P-101A/B, E-101 and FV-101
  3. Stations 8–9: C-101interface at grade, rotor and pressure on top
  4. Stations 10–12: outletsraffinate PV-108, analyzer shelter, extract

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • The 3-D plant is drawn from layout.json; the model runs behind it.
  • Twelve stations: solvent side, feed side, column, outlets.
  • Station 9 is the only climb: the EL 4.2 platform.

Part 2 · Field readings

What does each field reading tell you?

Part 2 · the plan

Know the normal value

  1. Normal readings at each stationdesign values and alarm limits
  2. How readings move with throughputwhat changes and what must not
  3. Reading holdup from PDT-110a pressure difference that counts drops

Interactive · pick a station (model at design, noise off)

The normal reading at each instrument

The route says where to stand; the model says what you should see.

A reading means little without its normal value; learn them station by station.

Interactive · model steady states at other feed set points (S/F 0.35)

What moves when the feed moves

Flows and PDT-110 rise, pump discharge pressures fall; pressure, interface and rotor stay put under control.

Interactive · local pressure gauges at the pumps (model steady states)

Reading a local gauge

A centrifugal pump gives less pressure at more flow: a low gauge at high rate is normal.

Derivation · what the active-zone ΔP measures

PDT-110 counts the drops

$\Delta p$
PDT-110 across the active zone
kPa
$H,\ \bar\varphi$
active height 1.8 m; mean dispersed holdup
m, –
$\Delta\rho$
drops against the column average, ≈ 300
kg/m³
$\Delta p\approx g\,H\,\bar\varphi\,\Delta\rho/1000$heavy drops add to the static head
$\bar\varphi=\dfrac{1000\,\Delta p}{g\,H\,\Delta\rho}=\dfrac{264}{9.81\cdot1.8\cdot300}\approx5.0\ \%$design reading 0.264 kPa

Interactive · read PDT-110, get the holdup (model points at 700–1200 kg/h)

More holdup, less flood margin

From the last slide$\bar\varphi=1000\,\Delta p/(g\,H\,\Delta\rho)$

On this unit PDT-110 and the flood approach rise together: a climbing ΔP is an early warning.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • Every field instrument has a normal value at design.
  • With throughput, flows and PDT-110 rise; pump discharge falls.
  • PDT-110 0.264 kPa means about 5 % holdup.

Part 3 · Valves and checks

How are hand valves and field checks handled on the round?

Part 3 · the plan

Check, compare, identify

  1. Hand valves at each stationthe normal state of each
  2. Field against the DCSreadings agree within 3 %
  3. Identifying the tagsname every box, target 90 %

Interactive · pick a station (hand valves in layout.json)

Check each valve against its normal state

A valve found out of its normal state is reported before anything else on the round.

Interactive · enter a field reading (rounds-sheet rule: within 3 %)

Does the field agree with the DCS?

Valves checked, now compare what you read with what the control room sees.

Outside 3 %, one of the two readings is wrong: report it, do not average it away.

On the Visual plant 3D tab

Name every box before the round counts

Switch labels

Labels to Identify: tags become blank boxes.

Pick the tag

Choose the tag for each box at every station.

Check

Target 90 % correct.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Sixteen hand valves, each with a normal state: NO, NC, LO or LC.
  • Field readings must agree with the DCS within 3 %.
  • Identify the tags to 90 % before trusting the round.

This deck

Key Takeaways

  • Walk the route in process order, station by station.
  • Know the normal value before you read the instrument.
  • Check every hand valve against its normal state.
  • Compare field and DCS readings; report a gap above 3 %.
  • Watch PDT-110: rising holdup means a shrinking flood margin.
